entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fakhr-un-Nisa Shuhdah Umm Muhammad al-Baghdadiyyah, a renowned Kurdish scholar, muhaddith, and calligrapher, left an indelible mark on the cultural landscape of the Islamic Golden Age. 

Born in the 11th century, Fakhr-un-Nisa's expertise in Islamic theology, hadith, and calligraphy earned her recognition as a prominent figure in Baghdad, a hub of learning and intellectual inquiry. Her contributions to the field of hadith criticism, a branch of Islamic scholarship that examines the authenticity and reliability of hadiths, were particularly significant. 

Fakhr-un-Nisa's work had a lasting impact on the development of Islamic jurisprudence and the study of hadith, influencing scholars for centuries to come. Her legacy extends beyond the confines of Baghdad, with her ideas and methods being adopted and adapted by scholars across the Islamic world. 

Despite the passage of time, Fakhr-un-Nisa's remarkable life and achievements continue to inspire scholars and students of Islamic studies, offering a testament to the enduring power of intellectual curiosity and dedication to the pursuit of knowledge.
